Qualitative finding: Useful solutions often remain embedded in threads or migrate to Slack, direct messages, private support, or local files. Strong post-mortems show that public canonicalization is achievable.
Bounded quantitative result: 29 of 55 purposively selected threads directly supported B1; no prevalence estimate. Canonicalization rate remains the intended outcome metric.
Strongest relationship: Hypothesized reduction in recurrence and clarification burden after publication of a maintained artifact.
Positive / negative case: The 50 µL tip post-mortem converted a cross-machine failure into dated diagnosis, merged corrections, and a reusable public record.
Primary community contribution: Resolved-knowledge index with version, applicability, evidence grade, supersession, and maintainer fields.
Prospective operational metric: Repeated-question rate and median clarification turns before versus after canonical artifact publication.
Evidence maturity: Strong qualitative; quantitative outcome not yet calculated.
Publication-safe claim: The forum repeatedly exposes a gap between solving a problem and preserving the solution as a maintained public artifact.
Main limitation: Private resolution and off-forum migration censor public outcomes.

Qualitative finding: Integration feasibility depends on discoverable documentation, usable APIs or protocols, licence clarity, isolated testing, examples, and identifiable maintenance. Driver existence alone is insufficient.
Bounded quantitative result: Mean IAS 63.9% across six bounded device–interface cases; isolated testing averaged 25%; 50% produced a positive public artifact or structured pathway.
Strongest relationship: B2–B7 phi 0.409, lift 2.157: interface accessibility is an enabling condition for orchestration.
Positive / negative case: PyLabRobot plate-reader support provides a public API, executable example, and contribution path; Cellario provides a structured commercial DDK.
Primary community contribution: Device-integration accessibility registry with component-level scores and version-bound evidence.
Prospective operational metric: Hours to first successful command, production-ready integration time, failed dispatches, and compatibility-recovery time.
Publication-safe claim: Public interface accessibility varies materially across integration paths and constrains which devices can be used reliably by higher-level orchestration.
Main limitation: Purposive cases do not support vendor rankings or reliability comparisons.

Bottleneck: Method, configuration, calibration, and runtime entanglement
Qualitative finding: Vendor environments frequently mix portable method intent with generated identifiers, internal databases, physical teaching, compiled artifacts, recovery workspaces, and active runtime state.
Bounded quantitative result: Mean RMC 54.2% across three deployment objects; 20.8% of applicable fields were fully bound, 62.5% partially represented, and 16.7% absent.
Strongest relationship: Mechanistic hypothesis: incomplete deployment identity increases execution ambiguity and recovery burden.
Short anonymized quotation: This is a runtime state file.
Positive / negative case: Community explanations identify VENUS file roles and source-control boundaries, but complete execution manifests remain absent.
Primary community contribution: Method and configuration bill of materials with immutable identifiers and explicit exclusions for transient runtime state.
Prospective operational metric: Cross-machine reproduction, rollback success, configuration-related incidents, and time to determine what changed.
Publication-safe claim: Versioning method source does not fully identify a laboratory deployment when calibration, external resources, software versions, and runtime state remain unbound.
Main limitation: Manifest completeness does not establish scientific reproducibility or correctness of recorded values.

Qualitative finding: Reliable physical resources require identity, geometry, coordinate semantics, nesting, material, tolerance, provenance, device validation, and sometimes independent reproduction.
Bounded quantitative result: Mean PDC 67.0% across four cases; median evidence grade 2.5/4; 50% device-validated; 25% independently reproduced.
Strongest relationship: B4–B8 phi 0.316, lift 1.781: representation credibility is coupled to validation.
Short anonymized quotation: This attribute has so far been completely missing in PLR.
Positive / negative case: The 50 µL tip case reached evidence grade 4 through cross-user failure, diagnosis, correction, and merged fixes.
Primary community contribution: Evidence-bearing physical-resource registry separating declared, measured, device-validated, and independently reproduced fields.
Prospective operational metric: Definition-related faults per 1,000 runs, cross-machine success, measurement disagreement, and correction latency.
Publication-safe claim: Physical-resource portability claims require both field completeness and bounded evidence about the device and configuration on which the definition was tested.
Main limitation: A validated definition is not universally portable; material and tolerance evidence are underrepresented.

Qualitative finding: Logs and telemetry are most useful when commands, observations, sample identities, state changes, interventions, recoveries, and outcomes are linked through stable semantics.
Bounded quantitative result: Mean OC 52.5% across four cases; 50% localized first divergence; none fully recorded final material or result disposition.
Strongest relationship: B5–B6 phi 0.452 and B5–B8 phi 0.424: strongest observed relationships concern recovery and validation.
Short anonymized quotation: Capture everything—and only surface what you need today.
Positive / negative case: Cross-contamination tracking translates material history into explicit state, although logical history is not a measured concentration.
Primary community contribution: Minimal laboratory-automation event schema with stable run, material, command, observation, intervention, and recovery identifiers.
Prospective operational metric: Time to diagnosis, incidents diagnosable without reproduction, final disposition completeness, and adjudicator agreement.
Publication-safe claim: Observability supports diagnosis and claim adjudication only when observations are linked to material identity, state transitions, interventions, and acceptance rules.
Main limitation: Telemetry volume does not establish physical truth or causal attribution.

Qualitative finding: Physical execution can fail after irreversible actions, leaving material in transit and software and physical states misaligned. Recovery must record material disposition and scientific validity separately from run continuation.
Bounded quantitative result: Complete-case PPR 66.7% across four scenarios; sensitivity 50.0%–75.0%; Wilson interval 20.8%–93.9%.
Strongest relationship: B5–B6 is the strongest pairwise relationship: phi 0.452, lift 2.353.
Short anonymized quotation: I might have valuable liquid in my tips.
Positive / negative case: A custom abort-handler example returns material under a bounded software-error scenario, showing that recovery must be scenario-specific.
Primary community contribution: Recovery incident record with irreversible prefix, last confirmed state, uncertain resources, permitted actions, actual action, and final disposition.
Prospective operational metric: Time to verified safe state, salvage rate, unresolved-state count, intervention burden, and recurrence after recovery.
Publication-safe claim: Selected incidents support a mechanism in which incomplete execution evidence constrains safe recovery after irreversible physical actions.
Main limitation: The pilot does not estimate laboratory-wide preventability or general recovery success.

Qualitative finding: Scheduler comparisons remain underdetermined when tasks, precedence, capacities, timing windows, stability, interruptibility, priorities, disposition, and failure policies are incomplete.
Bounded quantitative result: Weighted opening constraint completeness 53.8%; strict completeness 38.5%; discovery rate 87.5%; scenario-specific resolution 0%.
Strongest relationship: B2–B7 phi 0.409, lift 2.157: device accessibility constrains the executable scheduling space.
Positive / negative case: The toy problem generated a shared representation requirement for assets, timings, dependencies, and priorities.
Primary community contribution: Scheduler capability ladder and benchmark suite with fully specified scientific and operational constraints.
Prospective operational metric: Makespan, tardiness, expiry violations, resource utilization, replanning latency, and recovery after device failure.
Publication-safe claim: The forum is effective at discovering missing scheduling constraints, although the analyzed toy problem never becomes a fully specified benchmark instance.
Main limitation: Constraint completeness does not evaluate scheduler quality or optimality.

Qualitative finding: The term test is used across software, hardware, process, and assay levels. Claims become defensible only when the object, environment, acceptance rule, observed evidence, and scope are aligned.
Bounded quantitative result: Mean element completeness 73.3% across six bounded claims; 33.3% fully aligned; 83.3% at least partially aligned.
Short anonymized quotation: It may be called a functional test instead.
Positive / negative case: The VerisFlow 92/100 result is aligned when described narrowly as simulation-trace agreement; the 50 µL post-mortem is aligned to the documented resource failure.
Primary community contribution: Validation ladder and claim ledger binding each result to logic, interface, simulation, dry, wet, assay, or production-monitoring stages.
Prospective operational metric: False-pass rate, defect-detection stage, test–claim alignment, and adjudicator agreement.
Publication-safe claim: Simulation, software-state tests, wet-process tests, and assay validation support different conclusions and should be reported separately.
Main limitation: A high number of tests or a simulation pass rate does not establish wet or assay performance.

Qualitative finding: The finite command vocabulary understates the physical and organizational context required for executable methods. Community replies add substantial execution, validation, integration, data, and governance context.
Bounded quantitative result: Core CER 2.0×; broad CER 3.4×; conservative CER 2.2×. VerisFlow reports 92/100 simulation-trace agreement, Wilson 85.0%–95.9%.
Strongest relationship: B8–B9 phi 0.302, lift 2.316; strong within a five-thread AI stratum.
Short anonymized quotation: The human operator still needs to feed back the AI.
Positive / negative case: The forum narrows the VerisFlow claim to simulation evidence and explicitly surfaces missing wet, artifact-generation, and error-handling layers.
Primary community contribution: AI-method benchmark with missing-context tasks, required clarification behavior, and stage-specific evaluation.
Prospective operational metric: Human correction burden, physical trials, unsafe omission rate, wet-pass rate, assay-pass rate, and confidence calibration.
Publication-safe claim: The selected AI discussions show that method-generation performance must be reported by validation stage and evaluated for context completeness.
Main limitation: The context-expansion result is not an AI error rate and does not imply every context class applies to every protocol.

Qualitative finding: The dominant gap is rarely complete absence. Documentation is often undiscoverable, incomplete, restricted, version-specific, semantically opaque, or disconnected from examples, training, and responsive support.
Bounded quantitative result: Across 12 documentation-centered cases, 41.7% received fully actionable public resolution, 83.3% at least partial resolution, and 25% partly migrated privately.
Strongest relationship: Matched B2/B10 cases show negative descriptive correlation, but the measures share components and support convergent validity only.
Short anonymized quotation: This would have saved me so much time.
Forum reference: Ways to learn Hamilton HSL code? (Mar 2023)
Positive / negative case: PLR documents a low-friction editing pathway; vendor responses explain VENUS file semantics and current APIs in public.
Primary community contribution: Documentation-gap subtype dashboard and maintainership model with version binding, examples, correction path, and support ownership.
Prospective operational metric: Time to independent deployment, clarification turns, support escalation, link rot, thread revival, and maintainer concentration.
Publication-safe claim: The forum frequently converts hidden or opaque knowledge into actionable guidance, while persistent gaps cluster around detail, examples, support, access, and version currency.
Main limitation: Selected documentation cases do not estimate forum-wide documentation quality or user competence.
